topic: Diomede Islands — 2.4 miles apart, 21 hours apart in time
title: Two Islands 2.4 Miles Apart—But 21 Hours Apart In Time
description: AI-narrated commentary: two islands in the Bering Strait sit close enough to see each other, but the International Date Line puts them nearly a full day apart. #geography #shorts

hook_candidates.text: Two islands sit 2.4 miles apart — but 21 hours apart in time.
How can two islands 2.4 miles apart be a full day apart in time?
In the Bering Strait, two islands close enough to swim between live in different calendar days.
The International Date Line isn't a straight line around the globe — it bends specifically to split these two islands.

payoff_mechanism: The International Date Line usually follows a straight meridian near 180 degrees, but around the Bering Strait it deliberately bends westward to keep the entire political border between Russia and the United States on one consistent side of the line, so Big Diomede in Russia ends up a full calendar day ahead of Little Diomede in the U.S. even though the islands are only 2.4 miles apart.

beats.text: Two islands sit 2.4 miles apart — **21 hours** apart in time.
The **date line** bends here, to keep the border between Russia and the US on one side, not straight.
Little Diomede: US. Big Diomede: Russia. A full **calendar day** ahead.
**2.4 miles**, a full day apart — follow for more places where maps break.
